objective: Take up ROUND-READ-20261110-001's direction 4, given the go-ahead by the coordinator on 2026-11-10 (G1 with G5): does any drawn board make the route reading rounder than its own graph distance, or does the reading always equal the board's graph metric up to a constant? status: Complete 2026-11-10 (ROUND-READ-20261110-001's direction 4): proved that on every doubly periodic board of rings the route reading is a polygon norm up to a constant (classical, applied), so no periodic board's reading is round; computed that on the square, triangular, honeycomb and kagome boards at g = 2 to 6 the route polygon is the graph polygon scaled by 1/(g d/2), so the reading is the board's own graph distance times g d/2 up to a constant. The growth line's verdict: the reading is the drawn board's, scaled; the law adds scale, clock, offsets and a binary plain reading, no shape. Recommendation Full pivot.
